name: Planetary Mercury Incense
description: A planetary blend for the swift messenger, Mercury, ruler of speech, writing, commerce, travel and the clever mind. Traditional Mercurial herbs of the old herbals — lavender, fennel, dill and mastic-like resins — are combined into a light, quick-burning, airy smoke. Burn it on Wednesdays to sharpen wit and smooth communication.
steps: Cleanse your mortar and pestle and mixing bowl, then set out each ingredient and measure by parts (1 part can be a teaspoon for a small batch or a tablespoon for a jar).
Grind the resins first, alone, into a coarse powder; chill them in the freezer for 10 minutes beforehand if they are sticky.
Grind the woods, barks, roots and seeds next, then crumble the leaves and flowers by hand so they keep some texture.
Lightly crack the fennel and dill seeds rather than powdering them, so they release their scent slowly.
Combine everything in the bowl, mixing clockwise (or counterclockwise for banishing work) while speaking the chant and holding your intention.
Store in a labeled, airtight glass jar in a dark place and let it cure for 2 weeks before burning so the scents meld.
howToUse: Light a charcoal disc with tongs and wait until it is fully ashed over and glowing (about 5 minutes). Sprinkle a pinch (1/4 teaspoon) of incense onto it, adding more as the smoke fades. Burn on Wednesday, ideally in the planetary hour of Mercury, before writing, studying, interviews, negotiations, or setting out on a journey. Pass letters, pens or contracts through the smoke to bless them.
chant: Mercury, swift on silver wing, quicken the words my lips will bring; clear of mind and quick of tongue, let every message rightly run.
intention: My mind is quick, my words are clear, and my messages arrive.
timing: Wednesday, planetary hour of Mercury; waxing moon.
bestTime: Any season; especially late spring and early autumn (May–June, Aug–Sept), under Gemini and Virgo
caution: Burn only on a charcoal disc handled with tongs, in a heatproof censer filled with sand or salt, on a stable surface away from curtains, paper, hair and sleeves; never leave it unattended or fall asleep while it burns, and let used charcoal cool completely (several hours, or douse it in water) before disposal. Burning charcoal gives off carbon monoxide, so burn only in a well-ventilated room with a window open (never in a closed room, tent or vehicle), keep working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, and get to fresh air if you feel a headache, dizziness or nausea. Incense smoke irritates the lungs: avoid it if you have asthma, COPD or another breathing condition, and keep it away from pregnant people, infants and young children. Keep birds out of the area entirely (their lungs are extremely sensitive to smoke), let other pets leave the room, and store the loose blend where children and pets cannot reach it; never eat or drink it. Never add toxic plants (such as belladonna, datura, henbane, wolfsbane, foxglove, mandrake, yew or oleander) to incense, because their smoke can poison.
pets: Smoke is dangerous to birds and irritates cats' and dogs' airways: keep birds well away in a closed-off room and let pets leave. Keep the loose blend from pets, since lavender, mint and lemongrass are toxic to them if eaten.

name: Cleansing Smoke Blend (Smudge Alternative)
description: A loose, charcoal-burned cleansing blend offered as a respectful alternative to bundled White Sage "smudging", a sacred practice of specific Native American nations whose wild sage has been over-harvested for commercial sale. It uses widely grown European and garden herbs — rosemary, garden sage, juniper, bay, lavender and pine — that carry their own long smoke-cleansing traditions (such as Scottish saining with juniper).
steps: Ethical sourcing: grow these herbs yourself or buy organic, cultivated stock from reputable herb suppliers; avoid wildcrafted White Sage, Palo Santo and other at-risk plants, and never harvest from protected land.
Dry fresh herbs by hanging small bundles upside down in a warm, dark, airy place for 1-2 weeks until crisp.
Grind the frankincense to a coarse powder; crush juniper berries lightly; snip pine needles short.
Crumble the dry leaves and flowers by hand into a bowl and mix with the resin, stating that the blend is for cleansing and release.
Store in a labeled, airtight glass jar in a dark place; this blend can be used right away but improves after 1 week.

Open a window or door first so stagnant energy has a way out. Carry the censer (with a heatproof base or handle) through the space counterclockwise, wafting smoke into corners, doorways, under furniture and around people with a feather or your hand. Follow with a blessing incense or simply fresh air. This blend can also be used to cleanse crystals, tools and yourself.
